Retain the restriction to the four Article 1(b) categories, including the exclusion of ineligible oils. The label-only permission property is insufficient.
Power to prohibit domestic blend production for domestic consumption. The power is not itself a prohibition or permission to produce.
Member States cannot prohibit marketing on their territory of qualifying blends from other countries.
Member States cannot prohibit domestic production of qualifying blends intended for another Member State or export.
A Member State may set a packaging maximum above five litres for specified collective establishments, depending on establishment type.
Do not treat the qualifying brand/firm names as origin declarations. Preserve applications by 31 December 1998 under Directive 89/104/EEC OR by 31 May 2002 under Regulation (EC) No 40/94.
National power concerns extra virgin/virgin oils domestically produced from olives harvested domestically and intended only for the national market.
A national harvest-year decision must allow pre-labelled stocks to continue being marketed until exhausted.
Member States must notify the Commission of the harvest-year decision under Regulation (EU) 2017/1183. Actor-to-action duty needed.
Deletion of the no-limits pseudo-rule does not remove Table B purity obligations. No Table B rules supplied for review.
Represent repeals and reference substitution through the Annex III correlation table if these are in scope. They are not product-label duties.
Preserve entry into force twenty days after publication and applicability as legal metadata, if covered by the annotation protocol.
